A.summary: The booking flow has a clear hierarchy and follows the order patients need, with the appointment summary kept separate from the choices.

primary_focus.assessment: The page title identifies the task immediately, and treatment choices are the first substantial content. The confirmation action is prominent in the summary or mobile footer.

task_aligned_order.assessment: Treatment, practitioner, date and time, then patient details follow a natural booking sequence.

grouping.assessment: Numbered sections, dividers and local labels make each step distinct. Spacing within the date/time and details sections is relatively even, but their headings and control groups remain understandable.

alignment.assessment: Cards, section headings and fields follow consistent shared edges; the summary uses aligned labels and values.

structural_restraint.assessment: The form uses one main container and modest section dividers, although each treatment also needs its own selectable card.

focused_composition.assessment: The visible regions serve selection, entry or review; there is little unrelated content.

findings.observation: Four numbered sections move from treatment through practitioner and availability to patient details.
findings.why_it_matters: Patients can work through the booking in the same order they make its decisions.

findings.observation: Treatment cards, practitioner choices, dates, time slots and details fields are visibly separated into their respective steps; the desktop summary occupies a distinct adjacent panel.
findings.why_it_matters: Choices are easy to associate with the correct step while the current appointment remains available for review.

findings.observation: The page is limited to clinic identification, a short introduction, the booking form and appointment review.
findings.why_it_matters: Unrelated regions do not compete with the booking task.

B.summary: Normal content is scannable and efficiently arranged, but longer treatment text and prices do not consistently fit the tablet’s two-column option cards.

appropriate_density.assessment: Each treatment shows a name, duration, price and useful short description without excessive secondary material.

efficient_use_of_space.assessment: Two treatment columns use desktop and tablet space efficiently; the phone stacks options at a readable width. Longer option lists naturally increase page length.

clutter_control.assessment: Steps and morning/afternoon slot groups keep the larger set of choices navigable, including in the dense state.

content_fit.assessment: Default labels fit, but tablet cards with expanded strings have horizontal spill from titles and prices. A description and a summary value also spill slightly in the stress state.

findings.observation: Treatment options expose price, duration and purpose together, while dates and available time slots are separated into compact choice groups.
findings.why_it_matters: Patients can compare the information needed to choose an appointment without opening every option.

findings.observation: In the dense or pseudo-localized tablet states, six treatment-card headers spill horizontally by 7–58 px, including prices and a treatment name.
findings.why_it_matters: Names and prices are central to comparing treatments, and they become harder to read reliably in this required content state.

findings.observation: One treatment description and the selected-treatment summary value each extend about 4 px beyond their containers in the stressed tablet view.
findings.why_it_matters: These smaller overruns weaken the finish of the layout, though the text remains largely readable.

C.summary: The normal form and summary have coherent proportions, but expanded tablet treatment headers lose structural integrity when prices collide with neighboring text.

usable_sizing.assessment: Standard-state controls and fields are comfortably sized. At tablet width, the side-by-side form and summary leave too little room for some expanded treatment headers.

functional_proportion.assessment: The main form receives more width than the supporting summary on desktop and tablet; treatment cards are proportionate with normal text.

compositional_balance.assessment: The desktop composition gives the form visual priority and keeps the summary compact. The tablet retains that relationship, though its form column becomes tight under stress.

peer_consistency.assessment: Equivalent options and slot buttons use consistent geometry, and card heights accommodate wrapped descriptions.

structural_integrity.assessment: Normal states hold together, but expanded tablet option prices overlap adjacent labels.

findings.observation: On desktop, the booking form is the larger leading column and the narrower appointment summary sits alongside it.
findings.why_it_matters: Selection remains the main activity while review and confirmation stay visible without dominating the page.

findings.observation: In expanded tablet treatment cards, prices overlap neighboring option labels, covering substantial portions of the affected text.
findings.why_it_matters: This collision compromises the title-and-price structure patients rely on to distinguish and compare treatments.

D.summary: The interface generally adapts well across widths and keeps confirmation reachable, but the tablet layout is not sufficiently resilient to longer treatment strings.

adaptive_behavior.assessment: The booking layout and treatment grid change from two columns to one on phones; practitioner choices and slots wrap as space permits.

growth_resilience.assessment: Additional options and slots extend the page in a predictable order, but expanded treatment headers destabilize tablet cards as detailed under B and C.

priority_preservation.assessment: The booking steps remain ordered on small screens and a fixed phone footer keeps confirmation visible.

reachability.assessment: The form remains vertically reachable and the phone confirmation action remains on screen. Later phone dates appear to require horizontal scrolling.

scroll_behavior.assessment: Longer forms use ordinary vertical page scrolling. The partly visible fourth date hints at a horizontally scrollable date strip, though the interaction is not explained.

findings.observation: At phone width, the side summary is removed from the main layout, treatment cards stack, and details fields use the available width.
findings.why_it_matters: The principal booking steps remain legible and operable without squeezing desktop columns onto the phone.

findings.observation: A fixed phone footer keeps the confirmation button visible, including after validation messages appear.
findings.why_it_matters: The final action remains easy to locate as the patient moves through a long form.

findings.observation: The phone date row shows three complete dates and a clipped fourth, but provides no explicit cue to swipe for later dates.
findings.why_it_matters: Some patients may initially overlook additional availability, although the partial date offers a visual hint and the visible dates remain usable.

overall.reasoning: The standard desktop, tablet and phone layouts have a clear booking sequence, useful choice density and effective mobile stacking. However, in required expanded tablet states, treatment names and prices spill out of cards and overlap neighboring labels. Because identifying and comparing treatments is the first essential step, that failure materially degrades the experience despite the otherwise coherent layout.
